units.title: Vectors and motion
units.why: Vectors provide the language for direction-aware motion, forces and engineering design.
principles: resultant direction needs a reference axis
examples: 3 N east and 4 N north give resultant 5 N at 53.1° north of east
A displacement vector can be resolved into horizontal and vertical components

videoPackage.title: Thinking in vectors
videoPackage.transcript: We keep magnitude and direction together, resolve perpendicular components, and state the resultant relative to a clear axis.

units.title: Newton's laws
units.why: Newton's laws connect observed motion to interacting forces.
principles: third-law forces act on different objects
examples: A 5 kg cart with net 20 N accelerates at 4 m/s²
Weight mg acts downward while normal force acts perpendicular to a surface
misconceptions: third-law pair cancels on one body
practice: Identify forces on a resting book.

videoPackage.title: Forces on real objects
videoPackage.transcript: We isolate one object, draw only forces acting on it, select a positive direction, and add signed forces before applying ΣF=ma.

units.title: Momentum and impulse
units.why: Momentum explains collisions, safety systems and why stopping time changes force.
principles: total momentum is conserved in an isolated system
examples: A 2 kg object at 3 m/s has p=6 kg·m/s
Increasing collision time reduces average force for the same change in momentum
misconceptions: momentum is conserved for a system with external impulse
practice: Find impulse changing p from 2 to 10.
solutions: kinetic energy may not be conserved

videoPackage.title: Momentum through impact
videoPackage.transcript: We assign direction signs, track momentum before and after, and connect longer stopping time with lower average force.

units.title: Work, energy and power
units.why: Energy methods solve motion problems and evaluate machines without tracking every force.
principles: work changes kinetic energy when net work acts
examples: A 2 kg mass at 3 m/s has Ek=9 J
Lifting 5 kg by 2 m requires 98 J using g=9.8
misconceptions: power is the same as energy
solutions: positive when force displaces along direction

videoPackage.title: Energy methods
videoPackage.transcript: We choose an energy system, define reference levels, calculate stores with SI units, and compare energy with its transfer rate.

units.title: Chemical bonding and intermolecular forces
units.why: Bonding models explain why materials have different melting points, conductivity and solubility.
principles: ionic bonding involves electrostatic attraction of ions
examples: NaCl forms an ionic lattice of Na⁺ and Cl⁻
Water molecules are polar and form hydrogen bonds
misconceptions: intermolecular forces are the same as covalent bonds

videoPackage.title: Bonding and properties
videoPackage.transcript: We connect electron arrangement to ionic, covalent and metallic structures, then explain material properties without confusing bonds with intermolecular forces.
